selection_note: Thirteenth source-disjoint five-assessment screening cohort selected from the current included Index S1=A, S2=C records. All 60 sources in the preceding 12 merged manifests are excluded case-insensitively; no additional open Upstream assessment-batch PR was visible at selection. Prioritize source-specific S2 interference mechanisms and feasible offline first-party Python/Node tests; these are questions, not known bugs. Current public source heads and licenses were inspected. Screening is serial; no live models, provider calls, browser episodes, external fork/PR publication, Index regrade or autonomy claim.

candidates.finding: The assessed S2=C witness groups specialist jobs and rejects concurrent use of one connector. Check whether team-group admission and parent-chat uniqueness remain sound under competing starts or partial group-launch failure, using genuine first-party Python functions and fixed state without starting any model worker.

The assessed S2=C witness serializes and verifies shared session-memory updates. Screen current first-party memory.py plus test_memory_concurrency.py for a falsifiable lost-update or stale-write failure between separate sessions, with isolated files and no agent or provider invocation.

The assessed S2=C mechanism prevents two independently operating Actors from owning the same shared resource. Test the current first-party claims.ts admission/release path for conflicting versus disjoint resource claims and stale-owner handling with native isolated fixtures, without launching model agents.

The assessed S2=C witness uses a worker mesh and queue/pump to attenuate worker-node overcommit across Executor jobs. Inspect the first-party mesh, scheduling and release paths for inconsistent capacity admission or failure recovery under fixed offline Node fixtures, not live agent/provider execution.

The assessed S2=C constructor detects cross-run file overlap and routes affected plan commitments into an approval-gated adjustment. Test whether current first-party overlap analysis misclassifies create/delete or path alias changes and whether the unchanged plan is preserved when adjustment is withheld, using native deterministic fixtures only.
